question: The circuit forms a ( )-digit counter?

Using the day-length relation cos ω = –tan φ tan δ with δ = 23°26′, a 15-hour day gives B a latitude of about 41.4°N and a 9-hour day gives A a latitude of about 41.4°S, so the two places have equal latitudes on opposite sides of the equator. Final answer: 47°.

question: As shown in the figure, it is the v-t graph of two particles A and B doing linear motion from the same point. At time t=5s, how far apart are A and B?
cot_raw: The v-t graph shows two particles starting from the same point and moving together from rest to 4 m/s during the first 3 s; after t = 3 s, particle A (A) continues to speed up to 6 m/s at t = 5 s, while particle B (B) stays at 4 m/s. Displacement equals the area under the v-t graph. From 0 to 3 s, both particles travel the same distance: \(s_0=\frac12\times3\times4=6\ \text{m}\). From 3 s to 5 s, particle A travels \(s_A'=\frac{(4+6)}{2}\times2=10\ \text{m}\), and particle B travels \(s_B'=4\times2=8\ \text{m}\). question: In the region $0 \le x \le d$, there is a magnetic field perpendicular to the plane of the paper. In the region $x < 0$, there is a uniform electric field along the positive $y$-axis (not shown in the figure). A proton moves from point $P$ $(-\sqrt{3}d, -\frac{d}{2})$ with a velocity $v_0$ along the positive $x$-axis. At $t=0$, it enters the uniform magnetic field precisely at the origin $O$. The magnetic field varies according to the pattern shown in Figure (b), with the direction perpendicular to the plane of the paper and outward taken as positive. The mass of the proton is $m$, its charge is $e$, and gravity is negligible. 1. What is the magnitude and direction of the proton's velocity as it just enters the magnetic field? 2. If the proton exits the magnetic field along the $y$-axis within the time interval $0:\frac{T}{2}$, what is the minimum value of the magnetic induction $B$? 3. If the proton exits the magnetic field at point $M\ (d,\ 0)$ with the same velocity direction as when it entered the magnetic field, what are the magnitude of the magnetic induction $B_{\theta}$ and the period $T$ of the magnetic field variation?
cot_raw: In Figure A the magnetic field occupies \(0\le x\le d\), point \(M\) is at \((d,0)\), and the \(y\)-axis is the left boundary; Figure B shows the alternating field \(B(t)=B_0\) for \(0<t<T/2\) and \(B(t)=-B_0\) for \(T/2<t<T\), repeating with period \(T\). (1) In \(x<0\) the uniform electric field is along \(+y\). The proton travels horizontally a distance \(\sqrt3\,d\) at speed \(v_0\), so the time is \(t=\sqrt3\,d/v_0\); its vertical displacement is \(d/2\), hence \(\frac12 d=\frac12 a t^2\), giving \(a=v_0^2/(3d)\) and \(v_y=a t=v_0/\sqrt3\). Therefore the speed just inside the field is \(v=\sqrt{v_0^2+v_y^2}=2v_0/\sqrt3\) and the velocity makes an angle \(\theta=\arctan(v_y/v_x)=30^\circ\) above the \(+x\)-axis. (2) Inside the field the radius is \(R=mv/(eB)\). With \(B\) out of the page the proton turns clockwise and returns to the \(y\)-axis after a \(120^\circ\) arc, at time \(t=(120^\circ/360^\circ)(2\pi m/eB)=2\pi m/(3eB)\). For this to occur within \(0<t\le T/2\), \(2\pi m/(3eB)\le T/2\), so the minimum magnetic induction is \(B_{\min}=4\pi m/(3eT)\). (3) To exit at \(M(d,0)\) with the original direction, the simplest one-period path consists of two \(60^\circ\) arcs: a clockwise \(60^\circ\) arc under \(+B_0\) followed by a counterclockwise \(60^\circ\) arc under \(-B_0\). Each chord is horizontal with length \(2R\sin30^\circ=R\), and the total horizontal displacement is \(2R=d\), so \(R=d/2\). Thus \(B_0=mv/(eR)=4mv_0/(\sqrt3\,ed)\). The cyclotron period is \(T_c=2\pi R/v=\pi d\sqrt3/(2v_0)\), and because each \(60^\circ\) arc lasts \(T/2=T_c/6\), the field period is \(T=T_c/3=\pi d\sqrt3/(6v_0)\).
